text:
IncidentBot: paging @eng-oncall — elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate for eu region canary cluster (eu-prod-canary). Alert: 5xx spike, healthchecks failing on canary pods since 1937654280. Possible deploy just finished: release tag v2.3.1.
Sam Chen: ack. pulling logs now.
Maria Lopez: I'm in — I'm seeing CrashLoopBackOff for inference-canary- pods. Logs show config mount errors: 'failed to open /etc/config/model-config: no such file or directory' on startup.
Lee Patel: any recent manifest changes? I was on the deploy earlier — we changed configmap name to 'model-config-v2' but forgot to update deployment volumeMount name.
Sam Chen: that would explain the file missing. However why did HPA scale down to 0? kube events show scaling to 0 replicas around 1937654305.
Jenna K: HPA shows minReplicas: 0 for canary hpa object. I thought we always set minReplicas 1 for inference services.
Nikhil Rao: I pushed the HPA change in the same PR to tune down cost for canary. I must have set minReplicas: 0 accidentally. Sorry.
Sarah O.: we have a node drain in eu-1 ongoing from infra: 'drain for kernel patch' started ~1937654200. That combined with HPA min=0 allowed zero pods to be scheduled and traffic routed strangely.
Amrita (CS): customer impact — we see 5 enterprise customers with errors in EU region (error 502/503 on generate). CS is getting inbound support tickets. No data loss reported.
Sam Chen: mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag to disable canary routing (kill-switch) so prod traffic bypasses canary; 2) patch deployment to restore configMap name and rollout; 3) patch HPA to minReplicas:1 then scale deployment. Which is fastest?
Lee Patel: kill-switch first to stop customer impact. Then we can patch manifests and HPA.
DeployBot: rollback candidate available: v2.3.0. Ready to rollback if approved.
Maria Lopez: kill-switch command (internal flag service):
```
rdw-flag-client toggle --key=inference.canary.route --env=eu-prod --value=false --actor=maria.lopez
```
Sam Chen: I'm going to toggle now and route traffic away from canary. Will monitor metrics.
Sam Chen: toggled inference.canary.route=false at 1937654350 :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: action recorded: feature-flag toggled by Sam Chen. Notifying routing service to direct traffic back to stable pool.
Jenna K: since traffic is offline for canary, we're seeing error rate drop for customers. Good. Next: apply hotfix for deployment config to restore correct configMap name. Who can patch?
Nikhil Rao: I can push the manifest fix (change volumeMount to model-config-v2). Doing a hotpatch to canary namespace with image locked to v2.3.1 to avoid other drift.
Nikhil Rao: applying patch: `kubectl -n canary set env deployment/inference-canary --from=configmap/model-config-v2` — done. Pods are recreating.
Sam Chen: HPA still min=0. We should patch HPA to minReplicas:1 to ensure pods don't scale to zero during drain. I'll apply that.
Sam Chen: `kubectl -n canary patch hpa inference-canary-hpa --type=json -p '[{"op": "replace", "path": "/spec/minReplicas", "value": 1}]'` — applied at 1937654458.
DeployBot: rollback queued but not needed now.
Lee Patel: pods back to Running 3/3. Healthchecks green for canary.
Amrita (CS): customer impact update: support queue says errors largely resolved for the five affected customers; one customer still has intermittent failures but ticket updated. We'll continue to monitor.
Jenna K: infra node drain completed at 1937654700. No new evictions.
ena (oncall): I'll take the remaining watch window. Sam — can you do a brief postmortem doc pointer and assign owner?
Sam Chen: assigning postmortem to eng-runtime: will draft initial timeline and root cause (misaligned configmap name + HPA minReplicas 0 during node drain). Link will be added to the incident ticket.
IncidentBot: incident classified: SEV2 — canary caused customer-facing 5xx spike. Mitigation: feature flag kill-switch + manifest hotpatch + HPA patch.
Sam Chen: final status: mitigation complete, routing restored to stable, fixes applied, monitoring shows stable SLO for 20 minutes. I'll escalate to oncall rotation for followup.
Amrita (CS): CS to notify affected customers that root cause identified and fix deployed; offer post-incident call if needed.
ena (oncall): taking over monitoring. If any regression, page me with 'page oncall' @ena.
Sam Chen: thx all — postmortem will be circulated in ~2 hours. Closing thread for now.
